title: InfoGlobe: Local-and-Global Information-Preserving Statistical Manifold Learning for Single-Cell Transcriptomics
claim: A unifying geometric framework links count modeling, invariant metrics and factorization into one method that supports several downstream tasks.
layout: 5 panels (a-e), grid reading left-to-right, top-to-bottom, matrix factorization diagram in center
description: A multi-panel overview with five labeled sections. Panel a (top left) shows a cell icon and arrow labeled Random Sampling leading to wavy transcripts and a bar chart of observed gene counts. Below it, a count vector box and a pink multinomial distribution box with simplex-sum notation. Panel b shows a probability simplex triangle with colored cell points. An arrow labeled w=√p maps it to a Fisher-Rao hypersphere. A gold geodesic curve and a red dashed Euclidean chord are marked. Panel c compares Normalize+Log and InfoGlobe on a tetrahedron and a sphere. Blue and red path lengths are unequal in the first and equal in the second. Panel d, the largest, shows X = A × Z as colored heatmaps with sum-to-one constraint boxes. Below it are sphere embeddings and quarter-circle factor plots. Panel e (right) stacks three downstream demos: trajectory inference, batch-effect mitigation, and spatial domain segmentation.
caption: Overview of InfoGlobe. (a) Single-cell RNA-seq counts are modeled as samples from a multinomial distribution over genes. (b) The square-root transformation maps the probability simplex to the Fisher-Rao hypersphere, where Fisher-Rao distance is the geodesic distance. (c) Chentsov’s theorem identifies the Fisher-Rao metric as the unique invariant Riemannian metric under sufficient statistic-preserving transformations. (d) InfoGlobe uses Fisher-Rao geometry to factorize the cell-gene matrix into gene-to-factor and cell-by-factor matrices, both constrained on multinomial simplices. (e) The resulting factors and embeddings support downstream tasks such as trajectory inference, batch-effect mitigation, and spatial domain segmentation.
abstract: Geometry-preserving dimension reduction is critical for single-cell transcriptomics, where low-dimensional distances should reflect biological divergence between cell types along the transcriptomic manifold. Due to inadequate metrics, the global structure is not sufficiently preserved in the low-dimensional manifold in standard dimension reduction regimes. We model RNA counts as Multinomial samples, leveraging their hierarchical closure property: gene-level counts refine functional gene-group counts via nested Multinomial distributions. Extending Chentsov's Theorem, we show that the Fisher-Rao metric on coarse (gene-group) and fine (gene) statistical manifolds is isometric. Following this isometry property, we propose InfoGlobe, an information-preserving statistical manifold learning framework that projects cells from high-dimensional hyperspheres (full transcriptome) to low-dimensional hyperspheres (functional groups) while preserving information geometry. Embeddings on the low-dimensional sphere explicitly represent Multinomial distributions by functional gene groups. Benchmarks demonstrate superior preservation of local-and-global cell-type geodesic distances, automatic and robust gene-group discovery, nuanced cell subtype resolution without manual feature engineering and natural batch effect mitigation without explicit alignments.
